title: In-Situ Dynamics of Moiré Superlattice Epitaxy as a Platform for Site-Selective Adhesion and Growth
content: Precise patterning of atomic clusters, nanoscale islands, and molecules are required for the next-generation opto-electronic, energy, and quantum devices. While conventional ‘top-down’ methods, e.g. electron beam lithography, are now well-developed, limitations of resolution, cost and etching materials motivate the exploration of ‘bottom-up’ site-specific manipulation. Owing to the tunable electronic and chemical properties of their moiré landscape, twisted van der Waals (vdW) multilayers are emerging as a potential platform for autonomous domain-dependent assembly of atoms and molecules [1,2]. However, the underlying mechanism of this superlattice epitaxy remains phenomenological. Generalizability of moiré epitaxy across materials systems, length scales, and in a controllable manner would allow ‘bottom up’ assembly of atoms and molecules at arbitrarily small length scales and in pre-defined patterns.
